 VAR Set to Make Historic Debut in SAFF Championship 2026 Semi-Finals and Final
 The remote VAR system, operated from Thailand, will be introduced for the first time in the competition, beginning with the two semi-finals on November 14. By Rahul Giri November 12, 2026 No Comments 2 Mins Read

 The 2026 SAFF Championship will mark a significant moment for South Asian football, with the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) system set to make its debut in the competition during the semi-finals and final. The introduction of the technology is a first in the tournament’s history and is expected to bring greater accuracy to key refereeing decisions.
 The remote VAR system will be implemented in collaboration with the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), the ASEAN Football Federation (AFF) and the South Asian Football Federation (SAFF). Spanish technology provider Quality, a FIFA-certified company, will oversee its operation, with the central VAR hub located in Thailand.
 Under the remote VAR arrangement, live footage from Dhaka’s National Stadium will be transmitted to the operations centre in Thailand. Certified Video Match Officials will monitor incidents and assist the on-field referees in accordance with the International Football Association Board’s (IFAB) VAR protocol. Their recommendations will be communicated directly to the match officials in Dhaka.
 To support the system, a Referee Review Area (RRA) and a Technical Operations Team Area Monitor (TOTAM) have been set up at the National Stadium. Technical specialists from Quality are also working at the venue to ensure the infrastructure functions smoothly throughout the matches.
 The referees and assistant referees appointed for the semi-finals and final have undergone the necessary VAR training and certification, allowing them to operate within the established protocols.
 SAFF General Secretary Purushottam Kattel described the development as a landmark moment for the region, acknowledging the support received from the AFC and AFF in making the initiative possible.
 “The introduction of VAR is a groundbreaking moment for South Asian football and an important step towards raising the professional standards of our competitions. We are extremely grateful to the Asian Football Confederation and the ASEAN Football Federation for their invaluable support in helping us introduce this technology to the region,” Kattel said.
 He also stressed the importance of technology in improving the fairness and transparency of the game, adding that the move could encourage wider adoption of advanced refereeing systems across South Asia.
 India will face Bhutan in the first semi-final on November 14, while hosts Bangladesh will take on Pakistan in the second semi-final later that day. Both matches will be played at the National Stadium in Dhaka.
